questions: Did slalom progress rise above 0.39, or did any slalom run finish?
Did slalom line_loss_events fall back from 0.45 toward 0.05 at 0.45 kg?
Did s-bend steering_oscillation stay below about 0.55 (iteration 7: 0.487)?
Did oval and s-bend finish rates hold near 1.00 and 0.85?

intent: Keep the iteration-7 geometry (12 mm footprints, 7 sensors at +/-0.06 m, lead 0.05 m, 0.10 m track, body 0.12 x 0.10 m) and change only mass from 0.5 to 0.45 kg. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.39 with possible first finishes, oval finish at or above 0.95, and s-bend steering_oscillation below about 0.55. If s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.55 without a slalom gain, revert mass to 0.5 kg.
learning: Iteration 7 showed that the 12 mm footprint improves the oval and s-bend (finish 0.90 to 1.00 and 0.65 to 0.85) while leaving the slalom unchanged at max_error 0.062, and that it raises slalom line loss from 0.05 to 0.45. So sensor size is not the slalom limit, and the footprint is worth keeping. Mass is the remaining geometry lever with a demonstrated slalom gain, so the next step tests a further reduction. If it does not move the slalom, the limit is the controller's kd or base_speed, and I will hand that to the Integrator rather than change geometry again.
rationale: Iteration 7 (12 mm footprints, otherwise the iteration-6 design) is the best raced design at 645.9, up from 586.9. Oval finish rose to 1.00 (from 0.90) and s-bend finish to 0.85 (from 0.65), with s-bend steering_oscillation at 0.487, below the 0.55 revert threshold. The slalom did not improve: progress was 0.385 (vs 0.391), finishes stayed at 0, max_error stayed at the 0.062 floor, and slalom line_loss_events rose from 0.05 to 0.45. The footprint change is therefore helping the oval and s-bend, but it is not the slalom limit, and the extra slalom line loss suggests some edge jitter. I keep 12 mm, because reverting to 16 mm would give up the oval and s-bend gains. The iteration-6 finding was that lowering mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg raised slalom progress (0.34 to 0.39). The next geometry test is therefore a further, smaller mass step to 0.45 kg, which cuts yaw inertia by about 10 percent more. Expected result: slalom progress up to about 0.40 or more, with s-bend steering_oscillation staying below about 0.55. Risk: s-bend oscillation rises past 0.55 with the 12 mm footprint, which would mean the lower inertia is overshooting. In that case I revert to 0.5 kg with 12 mm.
